_: Round 422. `host-pins-plus.json` with twenty guardian labels repointed and NOTHING ELSE changed (round 435: the header said `nineteen` for thirteen rounds; `languages/whence/tests/test_checkpin.py::test_the_repointed_registry_changes_labels_and_nothing_else` has asserted `moved == 20` since round 423, and this file's own `repointed_from` field is present on exactly twenty of them) — no edit text, no witness, zero lines of examples/self_host.lang beyond the five checks the round added. Round 420's procedure, applied to the second guest file. A repoint is legitimate here only when the new label names the SAME mechanism as the pin, on its other side; `polarity.py audit` over this file must report 0 MISPOINTED, which is the non-circular half — pointing a pin at whatever happened to go red would guarantee `guarded` and measure nothing. ROUND 440 replaced that criterion, which round 438's next-step 1 assigned; the sentence above is kept verbatim because it is what rounds 422-438 measured against, and it fails as a criterion in two independent ways. (1) It is satisfiable by DECLINING TO DECIDE. Round 438 made both audit modes report `0 MISPOINTED, 1 precondition-broken, 4 undecided, 0 strict-violation`, and the 0 is reached by leaving four rows open. (2) It cannot see the hazard its own next clause names. `polarity.py repoint` draws every candidate from the pin's `co_red` list — the checks that ACTUALLY went red under that pin — so "pointing a pin at whatever happened to go red" is precisely the procedure that produced this file, and the score moved 1/20 = 5% (`run-plus.json`) to 20/20 = 100% (`run-repointed.json`). MISPOINTED is structurally blind to it: a check that went red under an edit is by construction not blind to that edit, so every repoint scores 0 MISPOINTED whether or not the new label names the same mechanism. THE CRITERION FROM HERE, in two parts, both currently FAILING and both re-derived by `languages/whence/tests/test_polarity.py`. (A) `polarity.py audit <this file>` must report 0 MISPOINTED **and** 0 undecided **and** 0 strict-violation — every directional pin POSITIVELY decided. `precondition_broken` rows are permitted and are the healthy outcome for a pin whose edit its guardian can see. Measured at round 440: `22 directional pin(s), 0 MISPOINTED, 0 unlocatable, 1 precondition-broken, 4 undecided, 0 strict-violation`, exit 1. The four open rows are CP03p (`broken_on_branch`, round 440) and CP06p/CP08p/CP10p2 (`undecidable`, round 438); the latter three are PROVED out of reach of any rule over the delta, so meeting part A needs a different instrument for them, which is round 438's next-step 5, not a better static rule. Passing `run-repointed.json` cannot change any of it — round 438 made the two modes byte-identical. (B) Every pin carrying `repointed_from` must argue about the guardian it NOW names. `repoint` moves the `guardian` label and nothing else, and `why` is prose about the guardian, so a repoint leaves the argument pointing at the old check. Measured at round 440: 20 of 20 repointed pins had a `why` byte-identical to their pre-repoint twin's in `host-pins-plus.json`, and CP03p's was measurably FALSE of its own guardian — corrected in place below, which is why the count is now 19 of 20. The other 19 are not asserted wrong; they are UNRE-AUTHORED, and nothing had said so. `test_the_repointed_registry_changes_labels_and_nothing_else` (`tests/test_checkpin.py`) enumerates the fields a repoint may not move and `why` is not among them, so this correction does not weaken it — but "NOTHING ELSE changed" at the top of this header now has exactly one exception and it is this one. `repoint_new_in_422` records whether the check the pin now names existed BEFORE this round.
